rows.author: K057;
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE FRAMEWORK FOR THE CONDUCT AND REGULATION OF ASSISTED REPRODUCTIVE TECHNOLOGY (ART) AND SURROGACY PROCEDURES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Proposes to establish a regulatory Commission to oversee the practice of ART and surrogacy to ensure that all parties involved in these procedures are fully informed of their rights and responsibilities - that appropriate safeguards are in place to protect the interests of all involved especially the child, and to ensure that accurate data are available on the number and outcomes of these procedures.
Proposes that a child born out of surrogacy procedure shall be deemed to a biological child of the intending couple and shall be entitled to all the rights and privileges available to a natural child.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2023-05-24

rows.title_full:
AN ACT INCREASING THE AUTHORIZED CAMPAIGN EXPENSES OF CANDIDATES AND
POLITICAL PARTIES, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 13 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7166, ENTITLED, “AN ACT PROVIDING FOR SYNCHRONIZED NATIONAL AND LOCAL ELECTIONS AND FOR OTHER ELECTORAL REFORMS, AUTHORIZING APPROPRIATIONS
THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES”
rows.title_short:
Increasing The Authorized Campaign Expenses Of Candidates And Political Parties, Amending For The Purpose Section 13 Of Republic Act No. 7166, Entitled, “ An Act Providing For Synchronized National And Local Elections And For Other Electoral Reforms, Authorizing Appropriations
Therefor, And For Other Purposes”
rows.abstract:
Increases the authorized expenses of candidates and political parties as follows: a.) For candidates - From ten (P10.00)) to fifty (P50.00) pesos for President and forty pesos (P40.00) for Vice-President; and from three (P3.00) pesos to thirty (P30.00) pesos for Senator, District Representative, Governor, Vice-Governor, Board Members, Mayor, Vice-Mayor, Councilor, and Party-List Representative for every registered constituent voter; and b.) For political parties - from five (P5.00) pesos to thirty (P30.00) pesos for every voter currently registered in the constituency or constituencies where it has official candidates.
Mandates the Commission on Elections, in consultation with the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, the National Economic and Development Authority, and the Philippine Statistics Authority, to make the necessary adjustments in the amount of authorized campaign expenses per registered voter as provided in this Act.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2023-08-16, transmitted to the Senate on 2023-08-22 and received by the Senate on 2023-08-22

rows.abstract:
Grants judiciary officials with judicial rank, salary and privileges to all retirement benefits being received by their counterpart judges and justices under Republic Act No. 910, as amended by RA 9946.
Entitles all those who compulsorily retired at the age of sixty-five (65) years prior to the effectivity of this Act including judiciary officials with judicial rank, salary and privileges, to receive the benefits under this Act, provided that the benefits granted shall be prospective.

rows.title_full:
AN ACT INSTITUTIONALIZING AND EXPANDING THE NATIONAL EMPLOYMENT RECOVERY
STRATEGY TO A JOBS CREATION PLAN AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract:
Intends to recover the labor market adversely affected by the pandemic - creates the Inter-Agency Council (IAC) for Jobs and Investments that shall formulate the Job Creation Plan (JCP)  with clear action components, success measures, and performance indicators regarding the following:  
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises ( M S M Es; unskilled workforce (youth and women); job and skills mismatch; employer/other private sector organizations/industry stakeholders that offer technology, upskilling, and reskilling; apprenticeship and other similar activities geared towards the improvement of the workforce; the transition of workers from the informal to the formal economy through business registration assistance; priority sectors, key and emerging industries and other areas with high employment potential to encourage domestic investment and financing direct investment;  active labor market policies, and progress (job matching services/digitalizing to reach more workers; participation/representation of the youth, women, and workers in the informal economy; social security and welfare benefits to workers in the informal economy; ethical and fair recruitment to protect the rights of migrant workers; national reintegration program for documented and undocumented OFWs.)
